name: Sub Bass
description: One-voice deep sine bass: a pure low tone that can start above its note and fall onto it, with added harmonics so small speakers find it, a soft drive and a long fade, for booms, held subs and slow soft pulses.

params.name: Shape
params.description: Bends the pure tone toward a rounder, squarer wave: fuller and more hollow, without getting louder and without losing any of the bottom.

params.name: Harmonics
params.description: Adds the octave and the fifth above it on top of the note, so it is still heard on speakers too small to play its bottom. The low tone itself stays as loud as it was.

params.name: Drop
params.description: How far above its note each strike starts before it falls onto it. A little is a soft knock at the start; a lot is a boom or a dive. A note slid to from a held one does not drop.

params.name: Fall
params.description: How long the pitch takes to fall onto the note. Short is a thump, long is a slow dive that lands exactly in tune.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How quickly the note comes up, from an immediate start to a slow swell.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long a held note takes to die away, from a short knock to a ring of many seconds. At the very top the note holds for as long as the key is down.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long the note takes to fade once the key is let go, from a quick stop to a long tail.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Soft saturation that thickens the tone and gives it an edge without making it louder. It bites hardest on loud notes and at the start of a note, and lets the tail go clean.

params.name: Glide
params.description: Time the pitch takes to slide to a new key pressed while another is still held. Keys played apart start on pitch.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it catches peaks at high settings.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. A sine from one double-precision phase, with the second, third, fifth and seventh harmonic added as polynomials of that sine (no filter anywhere), a pitch envelope that starts each strike up to three octaves high and lands exactly on the key, an S-shaped attack with an exponential decay or hold and release, and a seventh-order saturating curve after the loudness whose level loss is given back from the loudness and the drive setting. Tone and drive run at four times the sample rate (twice from 60 kHz up). Choices of this device, not measurements of anything: the proportions of the added harmonics, the shape of the fall (an exponential to a hundredth, cut off at the Fall time), the drive curve and how far a full-level note is pushed into it, one voice with last-note priority, and every new key striking the loudness again while only keys played apart drop. Tuned by measurement only: nobody has listened to it.
